title: Phase-conditioned intrinsic gap and inter-phase capacity split
question: Can the intrinsic kinetic graph be decomposed into within-phase coercivity and inter-phase capacity, so a broken-sector gap is not confused with a global tunnelling mode?
method: Sort the finite one-site q spectrum and define lower and upper sectors, leaving a possible central level as neutral mass.
For every reference Gibbs conditional row, compute the full momentum graph gap and the induced lower/upper sector gaps with the same conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi).
Record cross-sector capacity, neutral mass and phase masses separately over volume/cutoff, beta and both collar orientations.
Rebuild the finite model in an independent lane and use q-for-p plus cross-edge deletion mutations as hostile structural tests.
Compile Lean R405 for nonnegative sector masses, cross capacity and finite partition bookkeeping.
finding: The primary lane passes 1178/1178 assertions over 8 systems, 80 profiles and 1030 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 1088/1088, hostile 5/5, integrated 33/33 and Lean R405 compiles. Full intrinsic gaps range from 0.6310329497027756 to 6.229495058532403; the smaller induced sector gap ranges from 1.5773625260965005 to 20.555978652063708; cross-sector capacity ranges from 0.11650039514772156 to 1.222041249326006; the minimum phase mass is 0.010133814803601744 and neutral mass is at most 0.3870415227365262. The minimum full gap decreases from 1.0022812277674598 at beta 1/2 to 0.6310329497027756 at beta 8, while the induced sector floor stays near 1.58.
decision_reason: R-404 established a positive finite intrinsic graph gap but did not distinguish a global phase-switching mode from within-phase coercivity. R-405 makes that distinction explicit. The finite beta stress shows a softer global minimum than either induced sector minimum on this grid, so the analytic broken-sector route should target a phase-conditioned form and treat inter-phase capacity as a separate selection/tunnelling obligation. This is a route-local finite interface only.

adversarial_review.check: The lower and upper sectors are derived from the sorted physical q spectrum and any odd-cutoff central level is retained as neutral mass.
Each sector law is renormalized before its generalized eigenvalue is computed; unnormalized restrictions are not accepted.
Full and induced gaps are stored as separate fields and no finite inequality between them is promoted.
Deleting all cross edges exposes a second zero mode in the hostile representative, so the capacity cannot be omitted.
The q-for-p mutation has zero edges while the genuine momentum graph is connected with positive gap.
Finite Gibbs reference rows do not establish phase selection, cutoff/volume/source/exhaustion uniformity, a common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS gap or a physical mass gap.

next_action: Prove an analytic phase-conditioned sector Poincare estimate on one Hamiltonian common core, control neutral mass and cross-sector capacity under source and exhaustion limits, and only then transfer the sector form to the R-399 shell.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite phase-conditioned intrinsic-graph stress only. It proves no uniform sector gap, phase selection, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The finite separation is a diagnostic that distinguishes a potentially soft global mode from a within-phase scale; it is not a phasewise lower-bound theorem.
